## OMOP Common Data Model

::::::: columns
:::::: center
::: {.column width="75%"}
<!-- ::: {style="font-size: 80%;"} -->

The [**Observational Medical Outcomes
Partnership**](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/) (OMOP) Common
Data Model (CDM) is an open community data standard, designed to
standardize the structure and content of observational data and to
enable efficient analyses that can produce reliable evidence

<!-- ::: -->
:::

:::: {.column width="25%"}
::: {style="font-size: 75%;"}
![](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6570077?s=200&v=4){.r-stretch
width="98%" height="auto"}
:::
::::
::::::
:::::::

## OMOP Common Data Model

- The OMOP Common Data Model organizes data into **clinical event
  tables** (facts about a patient over time), a **person/demographic
  table**, and **standardized vocabulary tables**

- Every clinical fact is represented using a standard concept, which is
  why most columns end in `_concept_id` and resolve through `concept`

<center>![](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/man/images/cdm55.png){.lightbox
.r-stretch group="my-gallery" width="50%" height="auto"}</center>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## person {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
One row per patient, this is the anchor table every other table joins
back to via person_id
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `person_id` | Unique patient identifier (primary key) |
| `gender_concept_id` | Standard concept for sex/gender |
| `year_of_birth`, `month_of_birth`, `day_of_birth` | Birth date components |
| `race_concept_id`, `ethnicity_concept_id` | Standard demographic concepts |
| `location_id` | FK to `location` (address/geography) |
| `provider_id` | FK to `provider` (usual care provider) |
| `care_site_id` | FK to `care_site` (usual site of care) |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## observation_period {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
Defines the span(s) of time during which a patient's data is considered
complete/observable. Critical for cohort eligibility and
lookback/washout logic.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `observation_period_id` | Primary key |
| `person_id` | FK to `person` |
| `observation_period_start_date` | Start of observable window |
| `observation_period_end_date` | End of observable window |
| `period_type_concept_id` | How the period was derived (e.g., from EHR, insurance enrollment) |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## visit_occurrence {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
One row per patient encounter (inpatient stay, outpatient visit, ER
visit, etc.). Most clinical event tables optionally link back to the
visit during which they occurred.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `visit_occurrence_id` | Primary key |
| `person_id` | FK to `person` |
| `visit_concept_id` | Type of visit (inpatient, outpatient, ER, etc.) |
| `visit_start_date` / `visit_end_date` | Encounter start/end |
| `visit_type_concept_id` | Provenance of the visit record |
| `care_site_id` | FK to `care_site` |
| `admitted_from_concept_id`, `discharged_to_concept_id` | Admission/discharge disposition |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## condition_occurrence {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
Diagnoses - problems, complaints, and clinical impressions recorded for
a patient.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `condition_occurrence_id` | Primary key |
| `person_id` | FK to `person` |
| `condition_concept_id` | Standard concept for the diagnosis (joins to `concept`) |
| `condition_start_date` / `condition_end_date` | Onset/resolution dates |
| `condition_type_concept_id` | Provenance (e.g., primary diagnosis, billing code) |
| `visit_occurrence_id` | FK to the visit during which it was recorded |
| `condition_status_concept_id` | e.g., admitting vs. final diagnosis |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## drug_exposure {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
Records of drug utilization - prescriptions, administrations, and
dispensations.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `drug_exposure_id` | Primary key |
| `person_id` | FK to `person` |
| `drug_concept_id` | Standard concept for the drug (joins to `concept`, typically RxNorm) |
| `drug_exposure_start_date` / `drug_exposure_end_date` | Exposure window |
| `quantity`, `days_supply`, `refills` | Dosing/supply details |
| `route_concept_id` | Route of administration |
| `visit_occurrence_id` | FK to the visit during which it was prescribed/administered |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## measurement {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
Quantitative and qualitative clinical measurements - labs, vitals, and
other structured test results.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `measurement_id` | Primary key |
| `person_id` | FK to `person` |
| `measurement_concept_id` | Standard concept for the test (joins to `concept`, typically LOINC) |
| `measurement_date` / `measurement_datetime` | When the measurement was taken |
| `value_as_number` | Numeric result (e.g., lab value) |
| `value_as_concept_id` | Coded result, when the value isn't numeric |
| `unit_concept_id` | Unit of measure |
| `range_low`, `range_high` | Reference range for the test |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## procedure_occurrence {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
Records of procedures performed - surgeries, imaging, therapeutic
interventions.
:::

| Column                    | Description                        |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `procedure_occurrence_id` | Primary key                        |
| `person_id`               | FK to `person`                     |
| `procedure_concept_id`    | Standard concept for the procedure |
| `procedure_date`          | When the procedure occurred        |
| `visit_occurrence_id`     | FK to the associated visit         |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## observation {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
A catch-all clinical fact table for observations that don't fit
condition/drug/procedure/measurement - e.g., family history, social
history, survey responses.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `observation_id` | Primary key |
| `person_id` | FK to `person` |
| `observation_concept_id` | Standard concept for what was observed |
| `observation_date` | Date of the observation |
| `value_as_number`, `value_as_string`, `value_as_concept_id` | Result, in whichever form applies |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## concept {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
The vocabulary backbone of OMOP (Standardized Vocabulary). Every
`*_concept_id` column across every table is a foreign key into this
table.
:::

| Column | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `concept_id` | Primary key - the number stored in every event table |
| `concept_name` | Human-readable name |
| `domain_id` | Which clinical area it belongs to (Condition, Drug, Measurement, etc.) |
| `vocabulary_id` | Source vocabulary (SNOMED, RxNorm, LOINC, ICD10CM, etc.) |
| `concept_class_id` | Finer-grained classification within the vocabulary |
| `standard_concept` | `'S'` if this is the standard concept to use for analysis |
| `concept_code` | The original code within its source vocabulary |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Standard Concepts

- **OMOP** maps heterogeneous source codes (ICD-10, local lab codes,
  etc.) onto a single standard vocabulary per domain, so analytic
  queries only need to filter on standard `concept_id` values

- The `concept_relationship` and `concept_ancestor` tables support
  mapping between source and standard, and traversing concept
  hierarchies (e.g., "all descendants of Type 2 Diabetes")

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Connectivity of OMOP Tables

<center>![](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/man/images/cdm55.png){.lightbox
.r-stretch group="my-gallery-2" width="50%" height="auto"}</center>

Every clinical event table has a `person_id` (**who**) and usually a
`visit_occurrence_id` (**during which visit**), and every `*_concept_id`
resolves through `concept` (**what, in standardized concept term**)
